verdict.rationale: Proa templates are Rust macros: the macro "validates the template at compile time", component props passed in templates are "compile-time-checked", and editor tooling adds Rust hover, completion and go-to-definition inside the templates. Together these show type checking reaches into the template markup, not just surrounding code. missing for 10: an explicit statement that arbitrary expressions inside template slots are type-checked by the compiler, independent or hands-on corroboration beyond first-party claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get compile-time type checking inside my component templates, not just script blocks

citations.quote: The macro validates the template at compile time, consolidates adjacent static markup, and preserves the correct escaping behavior for dynamic slots.
the fields passed to AboutPage are compile-time-checked props.
Proa's editor tools add Rust go-to-definition, hover, completion, rename, and semantic highlighting inside raw-string `md!` and `md_sync!` templates
Adding a field or child to HTML can immediately flag its absence in a paired Markdown view, including when that view is not open.
